'''Judith Gabriella Berman''' is an American scientist, a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]], and a professor of [[genetics]] and [[microbiology]] at [[Tel Aviv University]]. She holds the Nathan Galston Chair in Antimicrobial Drug Research at the university's Shmunis School of Biomedicine and Cancer Research and is a professor emerita at the [[University of Minnesota]]. Her research focuses on fungal genome stability and responses to [[antifungal]] drugs, including how changes in chromosome number and genome organization contribute to adaptation in yeasts, particularly ''[[Candida albicans]]''. She is also an elected member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].

== Education ==
Berman received a Bachelor of Science degree in [[plant pathology]] from [[Cornell University]] in 1979.<ref name="BermanTAUProfile">{{cite web |title=Prof. Judith Berman |url=https://english.tau.ac.il/profile/jberman |publisher=Tel Aviv University}}</ref><ref name="BermanNAS">{{cite web |title=Judith Berman |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/judith-berman-7fjlk3/ |publisher=National Academy of Sciences}}</ref> She completed a PhD in [[biochemistry]] at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] in 1984 under the supervision of Ada Zamir.<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Judith Berman |url=https://en-pandemics.tau.ac.il/meet-Prof-Judith-Berman |publisher=Tel Aviv University}}</ref> From 1984 to 1986, she was a postdoctoral fellow in molecular biology and genetics at Cornell, working with [[Bik Kwoon Tye]].<ref name="BermanNAS"/>

== Career ==
Berman joined the Department of Plant Biology at the [[University of Minnesota]] as an assistant professor in 1986 and was promoted to full professor of genetics and cell biology in 2000.<ref name="BermanTAUProfile"/> She held an adjunct appointment in microbiology from 1999 to 2012 and was a visiting scientist in molecular genetics at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] in 2004.<ref name="BermanTAUProfile"/> In 2008, she was named a Distinguished McKnight University Professor at the University of Minnesota.<ref name="BermanMcKnight">{{cite web |title=Judith Berman |url=https://scholarswalk.umn.edu/university-awards/mcknight-distinguished-professors/judith-berman |publisher=University of Minnesota}}</ref>

In 2012, Berman moved her laboratory to [[Tel Aviv University]] and joined its George S. Wise Faculty of Life Sciences as a full professor.<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Judith Berman is Elected Member of European Molecular Biology Organization |url=https://en-lifesci.tau.ac.il/sbcr/news/2019/ProfJudithBerman |publisher=Tel Aviv University |date=2019-06-30}}</ref> She retained a research professorship at the University of Minnesota from 2012 to 2015 and became professor emerita there in 2015.<ref>{{cite web |title=Judith Berman {{!}} College of Biological Sciences |url=https://cbs.umn.edu/directory/judith-berman |website=University of Minnesota}}</ref> At Tel Aviv University, she directed the Joan and Jaime Constantiner Institute for Molecular Genetics from 2017 to 2023 and became director of the Strauss Family Genomics Research Unit in 2018. She was appointed to the Nathan Galston Chair in Antimicrobial Drug Research in 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=Award-Winning Scholars |url=https://en-lifesci.tau.ac.il/sbcr/AwardWinningScholars/?tab=18 |website=Tel Aviv University}}</ref><ref name="tau">{{cite web |title=פרופ' יהודית גבריאלה [ג'ודית] ברמן |url=https://www.tau.ac.il/profile/jberman |publisher=Tel Aviv University|language=Hebrew}}</ref>

In 2023, she was appointed an honorary professor at the Medical Research Council Centre for Medical Mycology at the [[University of Exeter]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof Judith Berman appointed as MRC CMM Honorary member |url=https://sites.exeter.ac.uk/medicalmycology/2023/06/22/prof-judith-berman-appointed-as-mrc-cmm-honorary-member/ |publisher=University of Exeter |date=2023-06-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230627100131/https://sites.exeter.ac.uk/medicalmycology/2023/06/22/prof-judith-berman-appointed-as-mrc-cmm-honorary-member/ |archive-date=2023-06-27 |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Research ==

Berman's research focuses on genome stability, fungal [[cell biology]] and responses to [[antifungal]] drugs. She has examined the organization, inheritance and variability of fungal [[genome]]s.<ref name="BermanNAS"/> Her earlier work investigated [[telomere]]s, the structures at the ends of [[chromosome]]s, including telomere-binding proteins in [[yeast]] and the relationship between [[chromatin]] assembly and [[gene silencing]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Enomoto |first1=Shinichiro |last2=Berman |first2=Judith |title=Chromatin assembly factor I contributes to the maintenance, but not the re-establishment, of silencing at the yeast silent mating loci |journal=Genes & Development |year=1998 |volume=12 |issue=2 |pages=219–232 |doi=10.1101/gad.12.2.219 |pmid=9436982 |pmc=316446 }}</ref> She has also studied [[centromere]]s, [[kinetochore]]s and the mechanisms governing [[chromosome segregation]] during [[cell division]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Burrack |first1=Laura S. |display-authors=etal |title=Neocentromeres provide chromosome segregation accuracy and centromere clustering to multiple loci along a ''Candida albicans'' chromosome |journal=PLOS Genetics |year=2016 |volume=12 |issue=9 |article-number=e1006317 |doi=10.1371/journal.pgen.1006317 |doi-access=free |pmid=27662467 |pmc=5035033 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Joglekar |first1=Ajit P. |display-authors=etal |title=Molecular architecture of the kinetochore–microtubule attachment site is conserved between point and regional centromeres |journal=Journal of Cell Biology |year=2008 |volume=181 |issue=4 |pages=587–594 |doi=10.1083/jcb.200803027 |pmid=18474626 |pmc=2386099 }}</ref>

Her research on ''[[Candida albicans]]'' has addressed [[aneuploidy]], in which cells gain or lose individual chromosomes; [[ploidy]], the number of complete chromosome sets; and [[loss of heterozygosity]]. These studies have examined how genomic changes generate variation within fungal populations and influence adaptation to environmental conditions.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bennett |first1=Richard J. |last2=Forche |first2=Anja |last3=Berman |first3=Judith |title=Rapid mechanisms for generating genome diversity: whole ploidy shifts, aneuploidy, and loss of heterozygosity |journal=Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives in Medicine |year=2014 |volume=4 |issue=10 |article-number=a019604 |doi=10.1101/cshperspect.a019604 |pmid=25081629 |pmc=4200206 }}</ref> In 2013, she co-authored a study showing that ''C. albicans'', previously considered an obligate [[diploid]], can form mating-competent [[haploid]] cells.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hickman |first1=Meleah A. |display-authors=etal |title=The "obligate diploid" ''Candida albicans'' forms mating-competent haploids |journal=Nature |year=2013 |volume=494 |issue=7435 |pages=55–59 |doi=10.1038/nature11865 |pmid=23364695 |pmc=3583542 |bibcode=2013Natur.494...55H }}</ref> Other collaborative studies have examined its [[parasexual cycle]] and the production of [[genetic diversity|genetically diverse]] descendants through changes in chromosome number.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Forche |first1=Anja |display-authors=etal |title=The parasexual cycle in ''Candida albicans'' provides an alternative pathway to meiosis for the formation of recombinant strains |journal=PLOS Biology |year=2008 |volume=6 |issue=5 |article-number=e110 |doi=10.1371/journal.pbio.0060110 |doi-access=free |pmid=18462019 |pmc=2365976 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hickman |first1=Meleah A. |display-authors=etal |title=Parasexual ploidy reduction drives population heterogeneity through random and transient aneuploidy in ''Candida albicans'' |journal=Genetics |year=2015 |volume=200 |issue=3 |pages=781–794 |doi=10.1534/genetics.115.178020 |pmid=25991822 |pmc=4512543 }}</ref>

Berman has also investigated the relationship between the [[cell cycle]] and fungal [[morphogenesis]], including the growth of ''C. albicans'' as yeast cells and [[hypha]]e.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Finley |first1=Kenneth R. |last2=Berman |first2=Judith |title=Microtubules in ''Candida albicans'' hyphae drive nuclear dynamics and connect cell cycle progression to morphogenesis |journal=Eukaryotic Cell |year=2005 |volume=4 |issue=10 |pages=1697–1711 |doi=10.1128/EC.4.10.1697-1711.2005 |pmid=16215177 |pmc=1265902 }}</ref> Her collaborative work has included [[genome annotation]], comparative studies of pathogenicity and reproduction among ''Candida'' species, and the development of genetic tools for studying protein function and [[essential gene|gene essentiality]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Braun |first1=Burkhard R. |display-authors=etal |title=A human-curated annotation of the ''Candida albicans'' genome |journal=PLOS Genetics |year=2005 |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=36–57 |doi=10.1371/journal.pgen.0010001 |doi-access=free |pmid=16103911 |pmc=1183520 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Butler |first1=Geraldine |display-authors=etal |title=Evolution of pathogenicity and sexual reproduction in eight ''Candida'' genomes |journal=Nature |year=2009 |volume=459 |issue=7247 |pages=657–662 |doi=10.1038/nature08064 |pmid=19465905 |pmc=2834264 |bibcode=2009Natur.459..657B }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Segal |first1=Ella Shtifman |display-authors=etal |title=Gene essentiality analyzed by in vivo transposon mutagenesis and machine learning in a stable haploid isolate of ''Candida albicans'' |journal=mBio |year=2018 |volume=9 |issue=5 |article-number=e02048-18 |doi=10.1128/mBio.02048-18 |doi-access=free |pmid=30377286 |pmc=6212825 }}</ref>

Another area of Berman's research concerns antifungal drug resistance and tolerance. Her collaborative studies have examined how fungal cells adapt to antifungal drugs through genetic and physiological changes, including the association between aneuploidy and drug resistance in ''C. albicans''.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Berman |first1=Judith |last2=Krysan |first2=Damian J. |title=Drug resistance and tolerance in fungi |journal=Nature Reviews Microbiology |year=2020 |volume=18 |issue=6 |pages=319–331 |doi=10.1038/s41579-019-0322-2 |pmid=32047294 |pmc=7231573 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=University of Minnesota |title=Researchers Discover Genetic Key To Treating Deadly Fungal Infections |url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2006/07/060721200644.htm |website=ScienceDaily |date=2006-07-22 |access-date=2026-09-10}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Selmecki |first1=Anna |last2=Forche |first2=Anja |last3=Berman |first3=Judith |title=Aneuploidy and isochromosome formation in drug-resistant ''Candida albicans'' |journal=Science |year=2006 |volume=313 |issue=5785 |pages=367–370 |doi=10.1126/science.1128242 |pmid=16857942 |pmc=1717021 |bibcode=2006Sci...313..367S }}</ref> This work has included research on the formation of [[isochromosome]]s that increase the [[copy-number variation|copy number]] of genes involved in drug responses, as well as how adaptation to one drug can alter responses to other drugs.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Selmecki |first1=Anna |display-authors=etal |title=An isochromosome confers drug resistance in vivo by amplification of two genes, ''ERG11'' and ''TAC1'' |journal=Molecular Microbiology |year=2008 |volume=68 |issue=3 |pages=624–641 |doi=10.1111/j.1365-2958.2008.06176.x |pmid=18363649 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Yang |first1=Feng |display-authors=etal |title=Aneuploidy enables cross-adaptation to unrelated drugs |journal=Molecular Biology and Evolution |year=2019 |volume=36 |issue=8 |pages=1768–1782 |doi=10.1093/molbev/msz104 |pmid=31028698 |pmc=6657732 }}</ref>

Berman has distinguished antifungal tolerance from resistance by examining variations in drug responses among individual cells within a population.<ref name="Rosenberg2018">{{cite journal |last1=Rosenberg |first1=Alexander |display-authors=etal |title=Antifungal tolerance is a subpopulation effect distinct from resistance and is associated with persistent candidemia |journal=Nature Communications |year=2018 |volume=9 |issue=1 |article-number=2470 |doi=10.1038/s41467-018-04926-x |doi-access=free |pmid=29941885 |pmc=6018213 |bibcode=2018NatCo...9.2470R }}</ref> This research has explored the association between tolerance and persistent ''Candida'' bloodstream infections, together with the effects of [[metabolism]] and interactions among [[microorganism]]s on drug responses.<ref name="Rosenberg2018" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Yu |first1=Jason S. L. |display-authors=etal |title=Microbial communities form rich extracellular metabolomes that foster metabolic interactions and promote drug tolerance |journal=Nature Microbiology |year=2022 |volume=7 |issue=4 |pages=542–555 |doi=10.1038/s41564-022-01072-5 |pmid=35314781 |pmc=8975748 }}</ref> She has also studied drug responses in ''[[Candida glabrata]]'', ''[[Candida auris]]'' and ''[[Cryptococcus neoformans]]'', as well as combinations of antifungal drugs.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ben-Ami |first1=Ronen |display-authors=etal |title=Heteroresistance to fluconazole is a continuously distributed phenotype among ''Candida glabrata'' clinical strains associated with in vivo persistence |journal=mBio |year=2016 |volume=7 |issue=4 |article-number=e00655-16 |doi=10.1128/mBio.00655-16 |doi-access=free |pmc=4981708 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Vatanshenassan |first1=Mansoureh |display-authors=etal |title=''Candida auris'' identification and rapid antifungal susceptibility testing against echinocandins by MALDI-TOF MS |journal=Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology |year=2019 |volume=9 |article-number=20 |doi=10.3389/fcimb.2019.00020 |doi-access=free |pmid=30834236 |pmc=6387932 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Stone |first1=Neil R. H. |display-authors=etal |title=Dynamic ploidy changes drive fluconazole resistance in human cryptococcal meningitis |journal=Journal of Clinical Investigation |year=2019 |volume=129 |issue=3 |pages=999–1014 |doi=10.1172/JCI124516 |pmid=30688656 |pmc=6391087 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bibi |first1=Maayan |display-authors=etal |title=Combining colistin and fluconazole synergistically increases fungal membrane permeability and antifungal cidality |journal=ACS Infectious Diseases |year=2021 |volume=7 |issue=2 |pages=377–389 |doi=10.1021/acsinfecdis.0c00721 |pmid=33471513 |pmc=7887753 }}</ref>

At Tel Aviv University, Berman's research received support through a [[European Research Council Advanced Grant]] for the RAPLODAPT project, covering 2014–2018,<ref>{{cite web |title=Ploidy change as a rapid mechanism of adaptation |url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/340087 |website=CORDIS |publisher=European Commission |access-date=2026-09-10}}</ref> and a Synergy Grant for the FungalTolerance project, covering 2021–2028.<ref>{{cite web |title=ERC Synergy Grants 2020: List of proposals selected for funding |url=https://erc.europa.eu/sites/default/files/document/file/erc-2020-syg-results.pdf |publisher=European Research Council |date=2020-11-04 |page=2 |access-date=2026-09-10}}</ref> The latter project, a collaboration with [[Markus Ralser]] and his team at [[Charité]]'s Institute of Biochemistry, investigates the mechanisms by which invasive fungal pathogens survive exposure to antifungal drugs across multiple levels of biological organization.<ref>{{cite web |title=ERC Synergy Project studies drug tolerance in intractable fungal infections |url=https://www.charite.de/en/service/press_reports/artikel/detail/erc_synergy_project_studies_drug_tolerance_in_intractable_fungal_infections/ |publisher=Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin |date=2020-11-05}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
* 1994 – Career Advancement Award for Women, [[National Science Foundation]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Award Abstract #9407704: Visualization of Chromosomal Telomeres in Saccharomyces cerevisiae |url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/show-award/?AWD_ID=9407704 |publisher=National Science Foundation |date=1994-05-16}}</ref>
* 2007 – Elected a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]<ref>{{cite report |title=AAAS Fellows |url=https://www.aaas.org/sites/default/files/AnnualReports/2007/aaas_ar_07l_Fellows.pdf |publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science |year=2007 }}</ref> and the [[American Academy of Microbiology]].<ref name="BermanTAUProfile"/>
* 2008 – Distinguished McKnight University Professor, [[University of Minnesota]].<ref name="BermanMcKnight"/>
* 2019 – Elected member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]].<ref>{{cite web |title=EMBO elects 56 new Members |url=https://www.embo.org/press-releases/embo-elects-56-new-members/ |publisher=European Molecular Biology Organization |date=2019-06-11}}</ref>
* 2023 – Foundation Lecturer, British Society for Medical Mycology; postponed from 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Meet us at the BSMM Conference |url=https://www.launchdiagnostics.com/news/meet-us-at-the-bsmm-conference/ |website=Launch Diagnostics |date=2022-08-23}}</ref>
* 2025 – Rhoda Benham Award in Medical Mycology, Medical Mycological Society of the Americas.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rhoda Benham Award in Medical Mycology |url=https://mycologicalsociety.org/rhoda-benham-award/ |publisher=Medical Mycological Society of the Americas}}</ref>
* 2026 – Elected member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="BermanNAS"/>
* 2026 – Elected member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |title=New Academy Members: Elected in 2026 |url=https://www.amacad.org/new-members-2026 |publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Berman and her husband Mike have two children together. In [[Twin Cities]], they were involved in the local Jewish community; their sons attended the Minneapolis Jewish Day School, and the Bermans both served on the boards of local Jewish organizations.<ref>{{cite web |title=Judy and Mike Berman Invest in Adath's Future |url=https://www.adathjeshurun.org/judy-and-mike-berman-invest-in-adaths-future.html |publisher=Adath Jeshurun Congregation|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260515234610/https://www.adathjeshurun.org/judy-and-mike-berman-invest-in-adaths-future.html |archive-date=May 15, 2026}}</ref>
